problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}-\frac{1}{z}\,dx+x\,dy+dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ for $t\in [0,\pi ].$

activity_context.topic_title: Sums of Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y Over Parametric Curves

feedback.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the circle parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,\pi ].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }-y\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-y\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\,dt \\  & =t{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\pi -0 \\  & =\pi \end{aligned}
$$
